title: Log the swallowed deleteAccountData Cloud Function failure in AccountManagementService._deleteFirestoreUserData (EH-3 log-less catch)
area: features/account domain service, tested from this batch's settings test tree

why: The comment claims 'Log but don't rethrow' but there is no AppLogger call anywhere in the catch body -- it is functionally empty. The Makefile's 'no empty catch blocks' grep (check 9/15) only matches a literal single-line `catch(...) {}`, so this multi-line, commented-but-logless catch is invisible to that checker (EH-3's 'log-less' half is explicitly Pending, not enforced). If the deleteAccountData Cloud Function fails during account deletion -- network error, quota, not-yet-deployed, permission-denied -- nothing is recorded anywhere (no Crashlytics, no Talker/AppLogger), so there is zero telemetry on failures of the primary Firestore-deletion path for a 'delete my account and my data' request. Verified account_management_service_test.dart has no test that stubs this call to throw and asserts on logging. The onUserDeleted Cloud Function trigger is a documented safety net that reduces the risk of the data actually surviving, but it does not restore visibility into how often the primary path fails.
recommendation: Add an AppLogger.error(...) call (uid only, no other PII) inside the catch block; add a test that stubs a throwing httpsCallable and asserts the log call fired.
acceptance_criteria: Catch block calls AppLogger.error with the uid and exception.
A red-first regression test in account_management_service_test.dart asserts logging occurs when the Cloud Function throws.
